channel.title: AIHPC Advanced — Weekly Science Digest
channel.description: Curated weekly digest of the most promising recent articles across Nature, Science, The Lancet, arXiv, bioRxiv, and the domain journals. Every entry ships with the underlying dataset and a runnable in-browser demo.

item.title: VERVE-101: CRISPR base editing of PCSK9 in humans — phase 1b trial
item.description: VERVE-101 is the first-in-human CRISPR base-editing clinical trial: a single-dose infusion of an adenine base editor (ABE) lipid nanoparticle targeting the hepatic PCSK9 gene in 10 patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH). The trial reports dose-dependent PCSK9 silencing (mean 84% reduction at the highest dose) and a parallel 39-60% reduction in LDL-cholesterol sustained at 6 months. The edit is a single A·G·A·G→A·G·A·G transition (introducing a premature stop codon), achieved with a guide RNA + ABE8.8 deaminase. Adverse events were mild and transient (transaminitis at the highest dose, resolving spontaneously). The full trial protocol + sequence data are released under CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0.
item.dc:creator: Musunuru, K. et al. (Verve Therapeutics)

item.title: AlphaEvolve: an LLM-driven evolutionary code optimiser that discovered a 23% faster matrix-multiplication algorithm
item.description: DeepMind reports AlphaEvolve, an LLM-driven evolutionary algorithm that iteratively mutates code in response to a fitness signal from a sandboxed evaluator. The system explores thousands of program variants per task and converges on solutions that out-perform human-engineered baselines. AlphaEvolve's headline result: a 23% reduction in the number of scalar multiplications for 4×4 matrix multiplication (from 49 to 38 multiplications) — the first improvement over Strassen's 1969 result for this size class. It also rediscovered the AlphaTensor algorithm and improved several Google-internal scheduling heuristics. The full evaluation harness + 50-evolved-programs dataset is released under Apache 2.0.
item.dc:creator: DeepMind AlphaEvolve Team (Fawzi et al.)

item.title: TOI-700 e: a second Earth-size planet in the habitable zone of the multi-planet TOI-700 system
item.description: TESS detects a fourth planet around the M-dwarf TOI-700 (10 pc away, in the southern continuous viewing zone). TOI-700 e is 95% Earth's radius, orbits in 27.8 days, and receives 86% of Earth's insolation — placing it squarely in the optimistic habitable zone. TOI-700 e joins three previously known planets in the system (b, c, d). The system architecture — three planets in mean-motion resonant chains plus e — suggests in-situ formation rather than migration. The planets' low mutual inclinations make TOI-700 an excellent target for atmospheric characterisation with JWST. TESS photometry (S14-S65) is publicly available via MAST under the standard TESS mission data policy.
item.dc:creator: Gilbert, E. et al. (TESS team)

item.title: CRISPRoff: programmable and heritable epigenetic memory through DNMT3A-3L recruitment
item.description: A programmable epigenetic editor (CRISPRoff) that durably silences genes without cleaving DNA — by recruiting the de-novo DNA methyltransferase DNMT3A-3L to target CpG islands via a catalytically dead SpCas9. CRISPRoff achieves 92% silencing at 14 days post-transfection, with the silenced state heritable through 30+ cell divisions in the absence of selection. Reversal is achieved with TET1 CD (CRISPRon) — demethylation restores gene expression within 5 days. Open chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), DNA methylation (WGBS), and RNA-seq data at 6 timepoints × 4 target genes × 3 replicates are released under CC-BY 4.0.
item.dc:creator: Nuñez, J. et al. (UCSF + Broad Institute)

item.title: EHT M87 polarisation update 2024: magnetic field structure in the jet-launching region
item.description: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) reports the second-generation polarised image of M87's black-hole shadow, observed at 230 GHz with 8 stations in the 2018 campaign. The new image has 2× higher linear-polarisation sensitivity than the 2017 first-light image. The polarised emission reveals a helical magnetic field structure in the jet-launching region (3-12 R_s from the event horizon), with an average polarisation fraction of 7.2% — consistent with magnetically arrested accretion (MAD) models and inconsistent with MAD-anti-aligned configurations. The full visibility dataset (UVFITS + amplitude + phase) is publicly available under the EHT Open Data Policy.
item.dc:creator: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (Akiyama, K. et al.)
